item.title: Trump decrees that anyone who uses the term Artificial Intelligence is now ‘The Enemy!’
item.description:
### Thank you for registering President Donald Trump on Thursday opened up a new front in his ongoing war against commonly used terms and geographic names by warning that anyone referring to Large Language Models such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT or Anthropic’s Claude as “Artificial Intelligence” would earn themselves a place on his enemies list.
Writing on Truth Social, he declared that the White House “considers anyone that uses the term, ‘Artificial Intelligence,’ as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, ‘Super Intelligence,’ THE ENEMY!”
The president’s outburst-cum-veiled threat landed just over a week after he signed an executive order directing executive branch agencies to begin referring to artificial intelligence, which is now embedded across the federal government, as “super intelligence” following a lunch [with leaders in the AI industry,](https://www.the-independent.com/bulletin/news/trump-ai-meeting-elon-musk-jeff-bezos-b3058451.html) including Elon Musk, Sundar Pichai, Dario Amodei and others.

item.title: Trump really wants to make ‘super intelligence’ happen. Is it going to happen?
item.description:
# Trump really wants to make ‘super intelligence’ happen. Is it going to happen? Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg speaks alongside President Donald Trump during a press briefing with AI executives, following a meeting on artificial intelligence, outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29.
## Superintelligence is a separate concept The term artificial intelligence has its roots in the 1950s, when a group of Dartmouth professors held a summertime conference “on the basis of the conjecture that every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it.”
In the theoretical evolution of AI, what comes next, he said is AGI, or artificial general intelligence, which refers to a system that has the same kind of learning and reasoning as humans, something Atman says might already have occurred.

item.description:

Chew’s remarks come as ByteDance, TikTok’s Chinese parent, expands its artificial intelligence research beyond consumer applications.
